item.title: Journalists Arrested After ICE Protest at Church, Raising Press Freedom Concerns
item.description: (AURN News) — Four people, including two journalists, were arrested following a protest at St. Paul Church against ICE enforcement. Former CNN anchor Don Lemon and independent reporter Georgia Fort were taken into custody by federal agents, along with activist Trahern Crews and Hennepin County Attorney’s Office staffer Jamael Lundy. item.title: Don Lemon Arrested in Connection With Minnesota Church Protest
item.description: (AURN News) — According to NBC News, former CNN anchor Don Lemon was arrested by federal authorities Thursday night in connection with a protest at a Minnesota church service earlier this month. item.title: Epstein Files: 3 Million More Pages Released, Trust Still Elusive
item.description: (AURN News) — The Justice Department has released millions more pages from its investigation into convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, calling it the final phase required under the Epstein Files Transparency Act. item.title: Menefee Secures Historic Texas Congressional Victory
item.description: (AURN News) — Democrats scored a major victory in Texas after Christian Menefee won the runoff in the special election for Texas’ 18th Congressional District. The historic seat was once held by the late Rep. Sheila Jackson Lee and most recently by the late Rep. Sylvester Turner. item.title: Partial Shutdown Underway as Immigration Standoff Freezes Parts of Government
item.description: (AURN News) — Parts of the federal government are shut down as Congress remains deadlocked over immigration enforcement following the deadly shooting of two U.S. citizens by federal agents in Minneapolis. The shutdown began Saturday but is far more limited than last year’s 43-day closure. item.description: (AURN News) — A federal judge has ordered the Department of Homeland Security to restore full congressional oversight of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention facilities, including unannounced inspections, after lawmakers were blocked from entering a detention facility in Minnesota. item.description: (AURN News) — Howard University announced that its Gallery of Art will lend three works to the Banneker-Douglass-Tubman Museum in Annapolis, Maryland.
